title: Teaching the Gospel of Jesus Christ (Part 2)
focus: Practice topic: baptism and the gift of the Holy Ghost
intro: After faith and repentance come baptism and the gift of the Holy Ghost, then a lifetime of enduring to the end. In this lesson learners study these doctrines and practise teaching them.
preparation: Study Matthew 3:13–17; John 3:3–6; 2 Nephi 31:17–20; and Doctrine and Covenants 20:37. Prepare a picture of Jesus being baptized and a short video of an invitation to be baptized. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: Baptism, our first covenant
paras: Show a picture of John baptizing Jesus and read Matthew 3:13–17. Ask partners: What truths does this account teach?

Write two words on the board: ordinance and covenant. Half the class studies the section on baptism for how to explain an ordinance, and half for a covenant. Ask them to define each word. Draw out the truth: baptism is an ordinance that we receive by authority and a covenant we make with God. Ask what we promise at baptism and what God promises. Study Doctrine and Covenants 20:37 together.

Read what Elder Robert D. Hales taught about baptism as total allegiance to God’s kingdom, and read Mosiah 18:9. Ask what it means, and how baptism could change a person’s life. Ask why immersion matters. It shows death to the old life and a new life as a disciple (see Romans 6:3–6).

sections.title: Being ready for baptism
paras: Read Doctrine and Covenants 20:37. Ask how it helps you know when someone is ready. Ask what it means to come forth with a broken heart and a contrite spirit, and how a person shows they have received the Spirit of Christ.

Give time to write how an investigator shows readiness. Show the video of an invitation to be baptized and ask what proved the man felt the Spirit and wanted baptism. Pairs prepare a short lesson on baptism using one or two scriptures. Two pairs team up, one teaching the other, and the learners say what they learned and how to prepare better for their missions.

sections.title: The gift of the Holy Ghost
paras: Share the Prophet Joseph Smith’s teaching that baptism without the gift of the Holy Ghost is only half a baptism. Ask what that means.

Tell about Nicodemus coming to Jesus by night and read John 3:3–6. Ask what Nicodemus misunderstood and how Jesus explained. Write: Born again. Born of water. Born of the Spirit. Ask what each means: being baptized by immersion and receiving the gift of the Holy Ghost. Read Moses 6:58–59 to see why the word born is used. Read the section on the gift of the Holy Ghost and ask what blessings come with it. Give learners a moment to think before they answer. Then pairs prepare a short lesson on the gift of the Holy Ghost, including one or two scriptures, and teach another pair.

sections.title: Enduring to the end
paras: Read 2 Nephi 31:17 and ask what Nephi called the gate. Read 2 Nephi 31:18–20 and ask what lies beyond the gate and what must follow baptism.
Ask why we must endure to the end. Draw out the truth: as we strive to endure, we qualify for eternal life. Ask how the Savior’s example helps us endure.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Define ordinance and covenant
examples.text: Write both words on the board. Give one simple sentence for each, then show how both apply to baptism.

examples.title: Show born of water and Spirit
examples.text: Read John 3:5. Draw two parts: water and Spirit. Say what each means.

examples.title: Show the gate and the path
examples.text: Draw a gate and a path. Use 2 Nephi 31:17–20 to show that baptism is the gate and enduring is the path.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Teach baptism in three minutes
examples.text: Define ordinance and covenant, read Doctrine and Covenants 20:37, and invite a person to prepare.

examples.title: Teach the Holy Ghost to a curious friend
examples.text: Show how to explain the gift of the Holy Ghost in simple words.

examples.title: Invite to baptism
examples.text: Show a kind, clear way to ask someone to be baptized on a set date.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Teach in groups of four
examples.text: One pair teaches baptism and the other teaches the Holy Ghost. Switch and give feedback.

examples.title: Answer a question
examples.text: A friend asks, “Why do I need to be baptized again?” Answer kindly with authority and covenant.

examples.title: Plan a baptism invitation
examples.text: Each learner writes how they would invite a prepared person to be baptized.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand baptism and the Holy Ghost? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in a few minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Testify that baptism and the gift of the Holy Ghost open the way to eternal life. Invite learners to share what they feel about their own baptism.

tips.text: Let learners write in a journal and reflect on what they studied.
Give a moment to think before a question that needs thought.
Display a quotation as well as read it. People understand better when they see and hear.
Divide the class into small groups and let pairs teach each other.

quote.text: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

study: Read 2 Nephi 31:19–20 together and ask what we must do after baptism.
invitations: Practise explaining the requirements for baptism in Doctrine and Covenants 20:37 and write two or three sentences about them.
Read the passages on the gift of the Holy Ghost in the manual’s scripture box and in the Bible Dictionary. Mark the verses that help you most.
Teach the gospel of Jesus Christ to a family member or friend, in person or online, and testify.

parts.title: The gift of the Holy Ghost

blocks.text: Write the two parts on the board.
**Share the Prophet Joseph Smith’s teaching that baptism without the gift of the Holy Ghost is only half a baptism.**
Ask what that means.
Tell about Nicodemus coming to Jesus by night and read John 3:3–6.
Ask what Nicodemus misunderstood and how Jesus explained.
Write: **Born again.**
Born of water. Born of the Spirit.
Ask what each means: being baptized by immersion and receiving the gift of the Holy Ghost.
Read Moses 6:58–59 to see why the word born is used. Read the section on the gift of the Holy Ghost and ask what blessings come with it.

Give learners a moment to think before they answer. Then pairs prepare a short lesson on the gift of the Holy Ghost, including one or two scriptures, and teach another pair.
How to run it: show one example first, then let pairs try it. Keep it to a few minutes and thank each learner.
Listen for: baptism and the gift of the Holy Ghost.
Say: “Born of water and of the Spirit.”
Draw the gate and path.
Read 2 Nephi 31:17 and ask what Nephi called the gate. **Read 2 Nephi 31:18–20 and ask what lies beyond the gate and what must follow baptism.**
Ask why we must endure to the end.
Draw out the truth: **as we strive to endure, we qualify for eternal life.**
Ask how the Savior’s example helps us endure.
Listen for: follow Christ, keep covenants, press forward.
Say: “Baptism is the gate. Enduring is the path.”

assignments: Read 2 Nephi 31:19–20 again at home. Write one thing it teaches you and be ready to share it.
Practise this topic with someone at home before next class: baptism and the gift of the Holy Ghost.
